gloss: time signal; hourly chime; time announcement

definitions.gloss: time signal; hourly chime; time announcement
definitions.explanation: A signal — typically a series of beeps, a chime, or a recorded voice — that announces the exact time, especially on the hour. Used by radio and TV broadcasts, telephone services, and clock towers.

examples.japanese: {時計|とけい}が{時報|じほう}を{鳴|な}らした。
examples.english: The clock chimed the time signal.

examples.japanese: ラジオの{時報|じほう}に{合|あ}わせて{時計|とけい}を{調|ちょう}{整|せい}した。
examples.english: I set my watch by the radio time signal.

examples.japanese: {毎日|まいにち}{正午|しょうご}になると、{町|まち}の{放送|ほうそう}から{時報|じほう}が{流|なが}れる。
examples.english: Every day at noon, a time signal plays from the town's loudspeakers.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{電話|でんわ}で「117」にかけると、{時報|じほう}を{聞|き}くことができた。
examples.english: In the past, you could hear the time signal by calling 117 on the phone.

notes:
{時報|じほう} literally combines {時|じ} (time) and {報|ほう} (report, signal). It refers to any signal that announces the exact time — whether a chime, beep, or recorded announcement.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時報|じほう}が{鳴|な}る: a time signal sounds
- {時報|じほう}を{流|なが}す: to broadcast a time signal
- {時報|じほう}に{合|あ}わせる: to set (a clock) by the time signal
- ラジオの{時報|じほう}: the radio time signal
- {正午|しょうご}の{時報|じほう}: the noon time signal

CULTURAL NOTE:
- In Japan, the noon {時報|じほう} broadcast through municipal loudspeakers ({防災|ぼうさい}{無線|むせん}) is a daily ritual in many cities and towns — a melody such as {夕焼|ゆうや}け{小|こ}{焼|や}け or a chime indicates noon and 5 PM.
- The classic NHK radio {時報|じほう} consists of three short "pi" beeps followed by a longer "pō" tone, marking the exact start of the next hour.
- The phone-based time service at 117, run by NTT, was widely used to set clocks before networked devices became common.

RELATED WORDS:
- {時|じ}: time, hour
- ドアチャイム: door chime
- {鐘|かね}: bell
- アラーム: alarm
